title: Introduce Invocation Health Index + alert escalator and lightweight streaming sample adapter
author: Evan Brooks
description: Summary: Adds an Invocation Health Index (IHI) that synthesizes latency, error-rate, token-cost drift, and KV-cache miss impact into a single 0-100 health score for routes and tenants; introduces an Alert Escalator which raises alert severity based on short-term IHI trend and a configurable business-impact model; ships a lightweight streaming-sample adapter that collects the first N tokens and key trace anchors for low-bandwidth trace capture; and adds dashboards and runbook snippets for on-call response. Motivation: existing observability artifacts capture many orthogonal signals (latency histograms, token cost histograms, span traces, kv-cache miss counters) but there is no compact operational signal teams can use to triage and automate alert routing/escalation. IHI provides a deterministic composite signal that is cheap to compute at ingestion and indexes into the escalation policies. What this PR does: - Compute IHI at ingestion using weighted, z-normalized submetrics (latency p95/p99 drift, error rate, token-cost delta from baseline, kv-cache miss rate) - Persist IHI as a metric label per-invocation and emit rollups (per-tenancy, per-route, per-model) - Introduce Escalator service that subscribes to IHI rollups and applies escalation policy (severity, paging, auto-ack suppression windows, SLA-aware dedup) - Add streaming-sample adapter in tracer pipeline that stores trimmed token payload (first N tokens) + span anchors to S3/short-term store for manual inspection; adapter is opt-in per-tenant and obeys PII redaction rules - Dashboards: Invocation Health Overview, IHI trend explorer, Escalation queue, Token sampling spot-check panel - Alert tuning: new alert rules that reference IHI sustained drops and modeled business-impact to adjust PagerDuty routing - Tests: unit tests for aggregator, integration test with local tracer adapter, load bench showing <0.6% ingestion overhead at 10k inv/s Checklist: - [x] Implementation: IHI ingester, escalator service, streaming-sample adapter - [x] Metrics emitted + tags added to rollups - [x] Dashboards and playbook snippets - [x] Tests and bench fixtures - [x] Docs: observability runbook updated and tenant opt-in docs added Rollout plan: 1) Deploy IHI ingester behind feature flag and emit metric to internal debug namespace 2) Enable per-route rollups for a small cohort of tenants (10 internal + 3 customers) 3) Turn on Escalator in alert-only mode (no paging) for 48h, tune thresholds 4) Enable paging for critical customers after sign-off Migration notes: No breaking API changes. Metric names and labels are additive. Tenants must opt-in for streaming-sample adapter; default is off. Privacy: token payload sampling enforces redaction pipeline and retention TTL. Impact: small ingestion CPU increase (~0.4 cores per 1000 inv/s) and additional short-term storage for samples. Links: runbook: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/OBS-2042-invocation-health-runbook, design doc: https://docs.redwood.ai/design/obs-invocation-health

b2c5e7a: implement escalator service and policy engine

review_conversation: Asha Patel (reviewer): Nice work, the IHI concept should help oncall signal clarity. Left two questions about normalization weights and the token-cost baseline window.

Evan Brooks (author): Answered — default weights are 0.4 latency / 0.3 error / 0.2 token-cost / 0.1 kv-miss. Baseline uses a rolling 7-day median by route; config is surfaced in config/feature_flags.yaml.
Miguel Torres (reviewer): Please add an integration test that demonstrates IHI stability during transient spikes (e.g., short 5-minute p99 spikes).
Evan Brooks (author): Added ihi_spike_sim in tests/ingestion; updated bench to produce synthetic jitter and validated stability.
Grace Lin (reviewer): Streaming-sample adapter must not persist full token text for PII-sensitive tenants. Add opt-out and redaction enforcement.
Evan Brooks (author): Adapter honors tenant opt-in and enforces redaction via rules in scripts/redaction/redaction_rules.yaml. Added tests and docs.
release_notes: Add Invocation Health Index (IHI): single-score health metric for routes/tenants
Introduce Alert Escalator: SLA-aware alert escalation and automated severity adjustments
Add streaming-sample adapter: opt-in low-bandwidth token sampling with PII redaction
New dashboards: Invocation Health Overview + Escalation queue
performance_impact: ~0.4 cores per 1000 inv/s for IHI ingestion; small storage for short-lived token samples
security_considerations: Sampling is opt-in per tenant; redaction rules applied to all sampled payloads; retention TTL enforced via GC job
rollout_notes: Feature gated: ihi.enabled and streaming_sample.enabled. Start with internal cohort, then staged customer enablement. Escalator starts in alert-only mode before enabling paging.
qa_notes: Run bench/ihi_loadbench to validate ingestion CPU and p95 latency. Use tests/ingestion/ihi_ingester_test.go for unit assertions. Verify redaction rules with scripts/redaction/verify_sample_redaction.py.
